reason: Re-opened Metzudat David on II Samuel 3:39 via packet.js --verse 3:39: under ואנכי היום he writes that even anointed over all Israel he is רך הלבב before the sons of Zeruiah, who are harder than he, ולפי שמן הדין אין ליואב משפט מות, שלא היו שם עדים והתראה, אולם ניתן רשות למלך לענוש לצורך השעה ... ולזה שמט ידו ממנו, כי לא היה יכול להם, ומסר דינו לשמים. Every clause of the reading (king entitled to punish where the law cannot, for want of witnesses; too weak to act; the judgement left to Heaven) is in his words at the place named. verse.js ok (2 Samuel 3:39, at [265,39]); entry-check ok (44 words). Plain sense checked against the day: 3:27 Joab kills Abner ‘for the blood of Asahel his brother’, 3:31 to 3:37 the mourning, 3:38 ‘the king said unto his servants’; the killing is stated in one plain clause (rule 6). Attacks tried and not landed: drift (the sentence gives ‘lacking witnesses’ where he says witnesses and warning, and ‘too weak against Joab’ where he says he could not prevail against them, the sons of Zeruiah; both are compressions that claim less, not more, and the judgement at issue is Joab’s, ממנו); plain (3:30 has Joab and Abishai slay Abner, but 3:27 has Joab strike the blow, so ‘whom Joab killed’ stands); attribution (Rashi gives only the Targum, Radak glosses ‘weak’ as new in kingship, no contrary reading to name); locator; school; comparison; tone; form.
better: Optional tightening: ‘yet too weak against Joab and his brother’ matches his plural להם; not needed to stand.
